_comment: WRITER DISPOSITIONS -- the hand-authored half of tools/gen_writer_attribution.py.
WHAT PROBLEM THIS SOLVES. SB-SOLE's release condition is that no ORIGINAL function writes a
region libmh writes. The census measures that population (188 live functions over 139 regions
today), and each one needs a terminal DISPOSITION: either a migration-ledger row that says we
own it (`verified`) or that nothing reaches it (`dead`), or an EXCEPTION with a named reason.
The ledger answers the first kind. This file answers the second, and only the second -- a
function that has a ledger row must NOT appear here, and the generator refuses one that does.
WHY NOT region_ownership.json's cross_write_accepted. That machinery adjudicates CROSS-SUBSYSTEM
writes -- a writer whose own subsystem differs from the region's declared owner -- and it is the
right tool for that question. It is the wrong tool for this one: 13 of MAP-LOAD's 25 writers are
map functions writing map-owned planes, so they AGREE with the owner, are not cross-writes at
all, and are structurally invisible to `gen_region_accessors --writers` (it filters to writers
that disagree, gen_region_accessors.py:324). An adjudication keyed on owner mismatch cannot
reach them. This file is keyed on `ours_writers` instead -- on whether OUR code writes the
region -- which is what SB-SOLE was re-keyed to on 2026-08-24 so that a re-attribution could not
narrow the scope.
AND NOT gen_state_registry's owned_by_dll rule, which is the other thing that looks like it
should cover this: it refuses an ORIGINAL WRITER ON AN OWNED REGION, but only fires on a region
carrying an `owned_by_dll` mark, and NOTHING carries one (0 of 738). It starts working when
SB-SOLE makes the first marks; until then nothing would catch a new writer appearing.
SCOPES ARE CHECKED ONE AT A TIME, and `checked: false` is not a waiver that can rot: the
generator FAILS a scope that is fully disposed but still marked unchecked, so an owner cannot
leave the gate off after doing the work. Unchecked scopes are reported with their live counts
next to the verdict, so the gate's coverage is visible rather than implied.

THE SPLICE-VS-TRANSLATE QUESTION WAS ANSWERED, as the scope required: TRANSLATE. Splicing the transition into the already-promoted emitter send_lockstep_resync_resume (whose only caller this is) would have left the two inline writes at 0x0043ee7e/0x0043ee88 executing, so the census would go on naming the function -- the item would have closed while the thing it was opened for stayed true.

U39.why: THE ONE GENUINELY OPEN WRITER on the whole frontier, and it is a fix rather than a translation: llm_ui_diplomacy_apply_and_resume writes Players[PlayerSide].relation[j] directly (22 bytes at 0x004c8070..0x004c8085) AND issues order 0xf4, whose handler libmh already owns. tracker/mp.yaml U39 NOPs the direct write under a guarded byte patch so the order handler is the sole writer. NOT excepted -- an exception here would accept a double-write on a HASHED cell (PLAYERS is in the hash manifest) -- and not owned either, because nothing has retired it yet. `checked: false` is therefore the true state: the scope exists so the writer is routed and visible, and it flips to checked when U39 lands. Its region PLAYERS is consequently the ONE region libmh writes that keeps a writer with no exception; region_ownership.json records it as such.

owned_elsewhere.DEAD_net_bwstat_accum_0049e8ea: SB-NET -- DEAD, and re-derived here rather than taken from the DEAD_ prefix, which is a name and not evidence. THREE independent scans of /eng/mh.exe at EN v379, all zero: (1) Ghidra's reference manager reports 0 references to 0x0049e8ea; (2) a raw little-endian dword scan of the whole 12.6 MB image for the literal address returns 0 occurrences, so it is in no function-pointer table, vtable, relocation or data word; (3) a byte-level scan of BEGTEXT -- the image's only executable block -- for E8/E9 relative CALL/JMP encodings computing to 0x0049e8ea returns 0 hits, which is the scan (2) cannot do since a relative call never contains the absolute address. Nothing reaches it, so its NET_BW_STAT write cannot execute. It surfaced as UNROUTED rather than UNDISPOSED because classify_fn has no subsystem for a DEAD_-prefixed name; this entry routes it AND disposes it. EXCEPT.

owned_elsewhere.llm_game_land_players_on_planet: SIM-RESID -- per-new-game landing/spawn logic, the same shape SIM-RESID already adopted for map_FillDefaults. For every enabled player it claims a landing spot, spawns an AI base or the human starting unit, then stamps STRAT_PLAYERS[i].primary_mother_unit, seeds STRAT_CTRL_GROUPS[0] with the new unit and sets the local base marker. STRAT_PLAYERS and STRAT_CTRL_GROUPS both carry ongoing libmh writers through a running game, so this is the FIRST write in that same series, not a disjoint pre-sim moment -- an init-only argument would be false here.
owned_elsewhere.llm_game_session_clear_system_presence_f: SIM-RESID -- elimination-check sim logic despite its Game/boot/misc name: its one write clears STATUS_ALIVE on STRAT_PLAYERS[2] when that player has nothing left in the system, which gates llm_strat_sim_step's per-player loop. It is reached from SwitchToPlanet, i.e. on every mid-game planet switch, not only at campaign start. The reason it cannot be excepted: libmh ALREADY has a translated sibling, mh::sim's llm_strat_player_presence_lost, clearing the identical bit under closely related conditions -- it is not armed today (no MH_EXPORT_REPLACE), and arming it would make this a second live writer of the same field by a separate code path. SIM-RESID should diff the two conditions for player index 2 rather than assume subsumption.

owned_elsewhere.llm_net_session_globals_reset: NET-SESSION -- the process-level lockstep bootstrap. One call from llm_game_init_subsystems (WM_CREATE) sets the pacing baseline the reimplemented turn engine then reads and mutates every tick: COMMITTED_HORIZON/HORIZON/STEP_SIZE = 10.0, ADAPT_NEXT_TIME = 70.0, SYNC_WAIT_ELAPSED = 1.0, PEER_TIMEOUT_ELAPSED = -1.0, GAME_SESSION_MODE = SESSION_MP_LOCAL, plus 8 counters zeroed -- 16 regions. In-process it is provably not a race (it precedes the boot-stage machine), but STANDALONE it is the mechanical reason it cannot be excepted: nothing else in libmh sets those constants, and a default-constructed 0.0 is not 10.0, so a standalone turn engine would start with silently wrong pacing.

The in-match MP diplomacy dialog writes Players[PlayerSide].relation[j] DIRECTLY (22 bytes at 0x004c8070..0x004c8085, ending in MOV [EDX+0xe587f1],AL) and ALSO issues order 0xf4 (llm_strat_order_set_player_relation), whose handler llm_diplomacy_set_relation is already translated as mh::sim::diplomacy_set_relation and shadow-armed. NOT owned by U39 and still O4-P's: whether a PROMOTED mh::sim::diplomacy_set_relation arms its effectful callees (llm_diplomacy_ai_relation_swap / llm_net_chat_ally_mask_rebuild) -- a handler that writes the byte but skips those is invisible at this cell either way. owned_elsewhere.llm_wait_screen_frame: NET-SESSION -- leader-local resync completion. In the mode-8 resync-wait frame it clears LS_RESYNC_WAIT out of NET_LOCKSTEP_STATUS_FLAGS and zeroes NET_RESYNC_IN_PROGRESS inline, which is byte-for-byte the transition libmh ALREADY owns for the receiving side: rx_dispatch.cpp's CTL_RESYNC_END arm (mp_leave_reset_game_mode / sync_busywait / clear LS_RESYNC_WAIT / time_resync_and_tick / resync_in_progress = 0), live by default. The promoted emitter send_lockstep_resync_resume only puts the packet on the wire; the leader's own local half of the same protocol transition is still original. Two implementations of one transition is exactly what SB-SOLE exists to stop, so this is ownership, not an exception.

load-path.why: IN-PROCESS (D4, docs/state-boundary.md): the host answers the bind table with the stock .bss base, so the original loader writes exactly the bytes libmh reads. STANDALONE the function does not exist -- and unlike TACT-WRITERS' mode-excursion class that is a REAL GAP rather than a no-op: these are the SOLE PRODUCERS of TILE_OBJECTS / PASSABLE / RESOURCES / MAP_REGION_GRID / STRAT_LANDING_SPOTS / HEIGHT / WIDTH, and a standalone libmh has no map-file reader, so it starts with empty planes. That belongs on LIB-REF, stated here rather than buried. RELOCATED-BIND BREAKS by construction: the original writes the stock base while libmh reads the relocated copy, so the planes arrive empty. Nothing exercises that today -- the same hazard (c) TACT-WRITERS already recorded on SB-HOSTFREE. SECOND ARM, ADDED 2026-09-10 (SB-SOLE / LIB-BOOT): the CONFIG-TABLE loaders, which hold on exactly the same in-process sentence and fail in exactly the same relocated-bind way. The eleven cfg_* constructors parse the unit/building/weapon/upgrade/project/system/planet/anim/text banks into their static tables in the single process-boot pass (ConstructObjects <- cfg_Init <- InitSafe <- llm_boot_stage_tick); libmh READS those tables and never produces them. STANDALONE this is the same real gap the map arm names -- libmh has no cfg parser, so a standalone host starts with empty config tables and must supply them; that belongs on LIB-REF and is stated here rather than buried. The cfg family is snapshot-imported by design, not pending translation (docs/reimpl-plan.md:45).

shared-scratch.why: The region is a TRANSIENT scratch cell -- a formatting buffer, a loader's file handle, a mask recomputed on entry -- whose value never outlives the call that wrote it. __Nan_Inf.why: THE WRITE IS NOT REAL, and `naming-gap` (the reason region_ownership.json carried until 2026-08-28) was the wrong diagnosis -- it asserts a subsystem-attribution problem where there is no write. This is the Watcom CRT float-formatting helper that emits "inf"/"nan" into the CALLER'S char* (0x00507388 = 69 6E 66 00, 0x0050738c = 6E 61 6E 00). At 0x004f434b MOV dword ptr [EAX],EDX the destination is a caller stack buffer; Ghidra's constant propagation instead resolved EDX's LOADED VALUE and minted ANALYSIS DATA refs on operand 1 -- one to DAT_00666e69 and one to 0x006e616e ("nan"), which lands inside MAP_REGION_GRID's 0x688ac4..0x708ac4 span. gen_state_matrix.py's pass B then took operand 0's WRITE ref-type for that target, because locate_operand cannot find a propagated value in any operand and the single-memory-operand fallback picks [EAX]. It is also NOT caller-less: _FtoS (0x004f36a3) and __cvt (0x004f438a) call it -- it looks orphaned only because call_graph_no_crt.json strips CRT edges. Extractor fix tracked in tasks/tooling.md.

llm_map_cam_set_col.why: NOT map-load. A pure setter -- MAP_CAM_COL := arg (0x0044af51), MAP_CAM_COL_PX := col<<5 (0x0044af5e), unconditional -- and it RUNS DURING PLAY, including from inside the deterministic tick: llm_strat_sim_step -> building_tick -> bldg_apply_damage -> bldg_state_destroyed -> spawn_debris_burst -> cam_jump_queue_clear -> cam_jump_queue_pop -> here, plus every strategic frame via llm_strat_input_update. Safe because ALL SEVEN libmh writers of MAP_CAM_COL are llm_tact_* (mission_start 0x00429281, tact_frame 0x0042a133, camera_center_on_tile, ui_order_buttons_minimap_tick, ui_sel_panel_multi_mode_tick, mission_load) -- tactical only, and llm_frame_dispatch makes the modes mutually exclusive. Positively: libmh's llm_strat_spawn_enemy_landing READS this global in strategic mode, so the original setter is the producer libmh depends on.  WHY THE STRATEGIC READER IS NOT A DESYNC, settled 2026-08-28 after the question was raised the other way round: llm_strat_spawn_enemy_landing (a `verified` T1 sim row) reads MAP_CAM_COL @0x00499954 and MAP_CAM_ROW @0x0049997c and writes _G_LLM_STRAT_PLAYERS @0x00499976 BETWEEN the two reads -- a sim write derived from where the local camera points, which is per-peer state. It reads the camera ON PURPOSE: it places the invasion landing OUT OF VIEW, taking the viewport metrics from `general` (@0x00e15398 / @0x00e153b0) between the two camera reads. It is SINGLE-PLAYER ONLY (user, 2026-08-28), so the per-peer input never reaches a lockstep-hashed write in a multiplayer session. STATE THE FORM OF THAT GUARANTEE PRECISELY, because it is not what one would assume: there is NO session-mode branch anywhere in the chain -- no function from llm_strat_spawn_enemy_landing up through game_HandleInvasion / llm_strat_invasion_chance_roll / llm_strat_invasion_due_check reads GAME_SESSION_MODE at all. The SP-only property is STRUCTURAL, from the campaign planet system: invasion_chance_roll gates on G_PLANET_INDEX < 0x1f and G_PLANET_STATUS == 2, and game_HandleInvasion on planet status plus planet_time. So the guarantee is 'a multiplayer skirmish does not run the campaign planet pipeline', not 'the code checks the mode'. If an MP mode ever drives that pipeline, this read becomes live and the camera is per-peer. AND THE DETERMINISM GATE WOULD NOT CATCH IT: both peers are driven through the same scripted path, so their cameras agree and the run cannot distinguish a camera-derived write from a deterministic one.

llm_strat_input_update.why:

THE ONE THAT IS NOT A CAMERA TIMER, and it is the reason this entry is not a one-liner: it writes STRAT_LOCKSTEP_HORIZON, a DETERMINISM-CARRYING region with seven libmh writers (lockstep dispatch/pump/force_resync/extend_if_near_horizon, order dispatch, order schedule, time_tick). llm_strat_render_bldg_docked_unit.why:
A RENDERER THAT WRITES SIM STATE, which is why 'it is presentation' is not the reason here. Measured: its ONLY non-read access to the 23,200-byte soldier array is `INC byte ptr [EAX + 0xe0e5c3]` at 0x00451955 -- a single-byte read-modify-write of one field, counted `rw: 1` with zero plain writes. That field is the per-soldier ANIMATION FRAME counter the draw advances as it walks the docked-unit sprites; everything else it touches (+0xe0e5ad/ae/bb/bf) it only reads.
libmh's thirteen STRAT_SOLDIERS writers are lifecycle and placement -- init_record, teardown, unlink, remove_last, set_heading, start_walk_anim, move_walker, squad_merge, transport unload, exit_ground. None of them writes the anim-frame byte. The fields are DISJOINT, so the two writers cannot race for a value.
Holds in any configuration. The check that catches it: a libmh soldier writer starting to touch +0xe0e5c3, which the state matrix would report as a second writer of that offset.

llm_strat_render_tile_object.why: The tile-object draw, and the byte-identical case to llm_strat_render_bldg_docked_unit: its only non-read access to STRAT_SOLDIERS is `INC byte ptr [EAX + 0xe0e5c3]` at 0x004524e8 -- the same single anim-frame byte, again `rw: 1` with zero plain writes, again reading +0xe0e5ad/ae/bb/bf only. Same disjointness from libmh's thirteen lifecycle writers, same check. LISTED SEPARATELY rather than folded into its sibling because they are two functions with two ref sites: if one is ever migrated the other's disposition must still stand on its own, and a shared entry would hide that.

llm_strat_selection_click_resolve.why:
The click-to-select resolver PRODUCES a selection; libmh only ever RETRACTS one. Its writes set the clicked target id, the selected building index and the control-group membership from the player's click. Every libmh writer of those three regions is a DEATH/REMOVAL path -- unmap_footprint, on_destroyed, remove_from_map, teardown, teardown_mapped, deploy_approach -- clearing the selection when the selected object stops existing. The two directions cannot disagree about a value: one names an object, the other un-names a dead one, and the sim never reads a selection to decide anything.
Holds in any configuration. Check: a libmh writer that SETS one of these to a live object id rather than clearing it, which would make the UI and the sim two producers.

llm_strat_selection_drag_finish.why: The drag-rectangle commit, and the same producer/retractor split as llm_strat_selection_click_resolve over the same three regions: it produces a multi-unit selection from the released drag, libmh's six writers only clear entries for objects that have died. Separate entry rather than shared: it is a different ref site with a different trigger (release vs click), and a migration of one must not silently carry the other.

llm_strat_ui_panel_init.why: Panel init CLEARS the 64-byte base-marker coordinate table at screen setup; the sole libmh writer, llm_strat_bldg_completion_dispatch, FILLS an entry when a base building completes. Producer and reset, ordered by construction -- panel init runs at screen entry, before any completion event of that session can be dispatched -- so the reset cannot erase a marker the sim has just written. Check: panel init becoming reachable mid-session (it is boot-stage-8 today), which would put the clear after completions instead of before.

llm_strat_ui_storage_bldg_panel.why:
A REDRAW REQUEST FLAG, single-producer/single-consumer. The storage panel sets pending when its contents change; the only libmh writer is game_SetEvent, which clears it as it services the redraw. A set that races a clear costs at most one extra panel repaint and can never produce a wrong value, because the flag carries no data -- it is one bit of 'look again'. Nothing in the order, save or hash path reads it.
Holds in any configuration. Check: the region acquiring a reader outside the panel/redraw family.

llm_strat_ui_unit_panel_tick.why: The unit panel's redraw-request flag, structurally identical to the storage panel's: this function sets pending, game_SetEvent is the sole libmh writer and clears it on service. One bit, no data, no sim reader; the worst outcome of a race is a redundant repaint.

THE EXCEPTION IS MECHANICAL AND IS STATED AS SUCH -- it rests on REGION EXPOSURE, not on a reading of this body: every one of them carries MF_VIEW only in mh_regions.gen.h, with NO MF_HASH and NO MF_SAVE, so those bytes reach neither the determinism hash the lockstep comparator reads nor a save file, and a lost or duplicated write there cannot desync or corrupt whatever the body does. The libmh counterparty is llm_game_start_tutorial and llm_tutorial_step_driver -- tutorial SCRIPT code driving the same menus, not a second authority over game state. Render/UI is a declared M6 non-goal (docs/reimpl-plan.md Sect. 1), so this stays original.

llm_ui_planet_select_screen_build.why: Writes 3 (menu frame) on entry while laying out the planet-travel screen -- the transition INTO a mode that is a mutually exclusive arm of llm_frame_dispatch's switch, so it cannot execute concurrently with mode 2's sim pump.

llm_ui_print_game_speed.why: sprintfs 'x%1.1f' into the 512-byte shared text scratch buffer and hands it straight to game_ui_PrintTextMessage. G_TEXT_TMP is reused by dozens of unrelated formatters across UI, sim, lockstep and tactical code, every one write-then-consume-within-the-call; no writer ever reads a previous writer's content. The region carries MF_VIEW|MF_MEASURED and NOT MF_SAVE (the evidence pack's in_save flag was derived from a serializer note, not the region table -- checked against mh_regions.gen.h directly), so nothing about the simulation can be read back out of it. sim_state.h already documents this exact buffer on exactly this reasoning.

llm_ui_selection_panel_refresh.why: Gated wholly on STRAT_UI_UNIT_PANEL_REFRESH_PENDING, which it clears on entry. Not a click handler: it is registered as a UI callback by a DATA write at 0x0051109c (1 DATA ref, 0 code callers). All five STRAT_UI_*_PENDING / VIEW_RESIZE_PENDING flags are UI dirty bits carrying MF_VIEW|MF_MEASURED and NO MF_HASH and NO MF_SAVE (mh_regions.gen.h), so nothing written to them reaches the determinism hash the lockstep comparator reads or a save file. The libmh writer of every one of them is the same kind of code -- game_SetEvent's reimplementation, which SETS the same 'please redraw' flag for its own UI events, and which is state:verified but promoted:false today, so no live conflict exists yet either. The worst outcome of a lost or duplicated write is one stale or one extra panel redraw.

llm_unit_ctrl_group_activate.why: The number-row recall that DOES switch selection -- the sibling of llm_unit_ctrl_group_flash_observer, which does not. Same producer/retractor split as the two selection functions: the keypress names a group as the live selection, libmh's writers clear members that died. Note this one is classed producer-consumer while its sibling is disjoint-fields, and the difference is real: flash_observer writes a per-UNIT byte, this writes the selection registers.

llm_unit_ctrl_group_flash_observer.why:
TWO REGIONS, TWO MECHANISMS, and the UNITS one is the load-bearing claim. Into the 186,400-byte unit roster -- 80+ libmh writers, the most contended region in the game -- it writes exactly ONE byte field: `MOV byte ptr [EAX + 0xdd8c77],0x0` at 0x0044a867 and `MOV byte ptr [EDX + 0xdd8c77],AL` at 0x0044a9e8, the unit's ctrl_group_id. It reads the same byte at three more sites and touches no other offset. No libmh writer of UNITS writes ctrl_group_id except the ctrlgroup add/leave/remove family, which is the same feature.
Into STRAT_CTRL_GROUPS it does a MOVS block copy (`movs: 2`) plus one rw: this is the recall-without-switching path, restamping the slot from group 0's live membership. libmh's four writers there are add_member/leave/remove_member/deliver_arrivals -- the same membership feature from the sim side, and they run at unit lifecycle events rather than at a keypress.
Holds in any configuration; the write is keyboard-driven. Check: a libmh UNITS writer touching +0xdd8c77 outside the ctrlgroup family.

llm_wnd_on_create.why: The Win32 WM_CREATE handler -- platform glue, a declared M6 non-goal -- with exactly one call site (llm_wnd_proc's uMsg==1 branch), firing once at process boot before any game session or mission exists. The libmh writer llm_tact_mission_start cannot run before window creation. Sequencing, not a field split, is the whole argument.

map_ReadMap.why: Map-file header parse. Writes width/height once (0x004a3340/0x004a334b) then calls llm_map_setup_dimensions. Sole caller map_ReadMap_pre, whose callers are SwitchToPlanet, llm_strat_planet_session_begin and llm_strat_session_begin_multi -- reachable from NONE of the eight llm_frame_dispatch mode roots. Safe rather than merely tolerated: libmh's only strategic writer of these two, llm_strat_planet_distance @0x00493fb2, is a SAVE/RESTORE SCRATCH (sets 100000 at 0x00493fe3/0x00493fed, restores at 0x00494013/0x0049401b), so the loaders are the sole durable producers of a value eight libmh readers consume.

_retired_by_translation._what: Exceptions RETIRED because the function became OURS, not because the argument was wrong. gen_writer_attribution refuses a function that carries both a verified ledger row and an exception, in those words: 'A function that is owned is not excepted -- delete one.' Kept here rather than deleted outright because each one's `why` is a real piece of RE (the call chains, the dominators, the self-restoring GAME_SPEED bracket) and the retirement is the interesting event: an exception is a promise that a writer stays original, and translating it is how that promise ends.

SwitchToPlanet.why: KIND init-only (planet-transition boundary), with one write of a different kind named separately. GAME_SPEED is a SELF-RESTORING BRACKET: saved, forced to 10x for a fast-forward drain loop, restored to the exact saved value before return, so the net effect at return is zero -- and the loop's real work already runs as libmh code, since llm_strat_time_tick and llm_strat_sim_tick are both MH_EXPORT_REPLACE'd. STRAT_GAME_CLOCK is rewound to the newly-active planet's own saved time only when switching to an unvisited planet -- a transition-boundary resync, which region_ownership.json already classes init-only, not a per-tick advance. G_PLANET_STATUS is DIFFERENT and is not covered by the init-only reason: the census-flagged store at 0x0044cef1 sits in a block Ghidra marks unreachable (the value stored at 0x0044cedc is compared against 0 and branched away at 0x0044cee3), and region_ownership.json already carries that dead-store diagnosis with the same addresses; this function's only live access to that region is a read.

llm_map_assign_remaining_tiles_to_region.why: Second-pass labeller (0x00422b36). Sole caller llm_map_seed_regions_multires <- llm_map_build_regions. Safe because libmh's five MAP_REGION_GRID writers (region_split, merge_small_regions, region_apply_area, map_ApplyAreaToMap, region_flood_reachable) are all MUTATORS of an already-built grid, reached from group-move pathfinding at play time -- they require this builder's output.

llm_map_build_regions.why: Region-decomposition driver (0x004233f2/0x0042340c/0x004234a4). Sole callers llm_map_load_passable_plane / _loose, both dominated by map_ReadMap. Not reachable from any of the eight frame roots.

llm_map_compute_obstacle_proximity_flags.why: Writes the grid's second dword (MOV [+0x688ac8],EDX @0x004220e9). Sole caller llm_map_build_regions, inheriting its chain.

llm_map_region_flood_fill.why: Flood-labels a region (0x00422487, 0x0042259b, 0x00422684). Callers llm_map_assign_remaining_tiles_to_regions and llm_map_try_seed_region_at, both under llm_map_seed_regions_multires <- llm_map_build_regions.

llm_map_seed_regions_multires.why: Map-file load seeds the region pool the LT1C allocator owns at runtime -- the same class as MAP-LOAD's other excepted writers (LIB-WORLD: map loading stays excluded pre-fork; the standalone host imports a world blob instead). (Surfaced by the 2026-09-02 lib_trans domain-close accessor-census refresh: the regions were registered at LT-READY/LT0 and their libmh writers landed in LT1C/LT1D, so these ORIGINAL co-writers became attributable for the first time.)
